title: Ecosystem command surface (one file per ecosystem)
description: Schema for a consuming repository's docs/conventions/ecosystems/<ecosystem>.yaml file. The filename stem is the ecosystem identifier (lowercase kebab-case). Command values are opaque shell strings; null means the ecosystem has no such phase. Contract: docs/contracts/ecosystem-commands/README.md.

enabled.description: Whether this ecosystem applies to the repo. False disables detection without deleting the file.

globs.description: File glob patterns that classify changed files into this ecosystem (matched against repo-relative paths).

anchor.description: How to resolve <solution-or-project-file>: the scoping anchor for ecosystems with a canonical entry point (e.g. 'the solution file at repo root (*.slnx)').

project-discovery.description: File patterns identifying per-project roots (walked for <project-dir>), e.g. ['pyproject.toml'].

build-cmd.description: Build/compile verification command. Null when the ecosystem has no build step.

test-cmd.description: Test command. Null when no test framework is wired.

test-changed-cmd.description: Change-scoped test command over <files>: runs the tests the changed files select. /toolchain:check runs it for a change and test-cmd under all; CI calls the same recorded command. Null or absent when the repository has no change-scoped test command.

check-cmd.description: Lint/format check command (no file modification). Null when lint does not apply.

lint-cmd.description: Report-only lint command (no file modification, no format check). /toolchain:lint and /toolchain:check run it in place of check-cmd when it is set; no hook runs it. Null or absent when the repository has no separate lint command.

fix-cmd.description: Format-only auto-fix command (whitespace, import layout, style). Must not apply semantic/code-changing lint autofixes. Null when the toolchain has no format-fix mode. Code-changing autofixes belong in code-fix-cmd.

code-fix-cmd.description: Code-changing auto-fix command (lint autofixes that rewrite logic, delete unused imports, apply safe/unsafe code edits). Null when absent. Invoked only by /toolchain:lint --code-fix behind that skill's confirmation / --yes gate — never by bare --fix.

opt-in.description: A condition resolvers evaluate to decide whether to run this ecosystem's lint phase — either a single condition governing the whole check-cmd (e.g. 'a ruff config (ruff.toml, .ruff.toml, or pyproject.toml [tool.ruff])'), or a multi-clause value where each clause names a sub-tool and its own condition (e.g. 'shellcheck always applies to shell files; shfmt only when .editorconfig declares shell style'). Unmet -> resolvers report a visible skip rather than silently omitting the ecosystem, and never impose the tool's built-in defaults on a repo that hasn't configured it.

install-hint.description: Cross-platform install guidance shown when a required tool is missing. Missing tools report skip, never failure.

tool-pin.description: Pinned tool versions keyed by tool name. When present, resolvers warn if the installed version drifts from the pin. Set only for a tool whose version the repository owns itself (a manifest, lockfile, or version input its own workflow sets); omit it when the version comes from a shared default, since a copy drifts. Inert when absent.

requires.description: What a command needs beyond the tool it is invoked through being on PATH, keyed by command key: a runtime package that must be installed, or a tool at the build the repo pins for CI. Before a resolver runs a command it runs each entry's probe; when any entry is absent, the command does not run and its cell reads skip (prerequisite missing: <name>), an environment skip that keeps the run from reading PASS. One missing entry skips the whole command, every tool bundled in its string included. Resolvers never install a declared prerequisite.

gates.description: Repo-specific CI-parity gates beyond plain build/test/lint (lockfile drift, generated-artifact freshness, schema regeneration).

trigger-globs.description: Run the gate only when a changed file matches (matched against the full changed-file set); omit to run whenever the ecosystem runs. Never selects the ecosystem under auto-targeting — to make a cross-ecosystem trigger select its ecosystem, add the pattern to the ecosystem's own `globs`.

run-from.description: Execution scope for this gate's cmd. 'ecosystem' (default) runs from the same location the ecosystem's own build/test/lint use — once per project-discovery root, the anchor's directory, or $REPO_ROOT when neither is defined; unchanged from pre-run-from behavior. 'repo-root' forces a single run from $REPO_ROOT regardless of the ecosystem's project-discovery or anchor, for a repo-wide check (e.g. protobuf generation, schema freshness) declared under a project-discovery ecosystem that would otherwise run redundantly, or fail, once per project root. Under 'repo-root', a cmd using the <files> placeholder gets the full ecosystem-scoped changed-files set, not one project's subset, and <project-dir> is undefined — a cmd using it under 'repo-root' is a configuration error a resolver reports as a failure rather than guessing an expansion.

requires.description: What this gate's cmd needs beyond its tool on PATH, with the same meaning as a top-level requires entry: any absent entry reports the gate as skip (prerequisite missing: <name>) and its cmd does not run.

notes.description: Free-form caveats a resolver should surface (trap flags, ordering constraints). Rationale belongs in the repo's own rules, not here.

name.description: What the command needs, as the skip cell names it: skip (prerequisite missing: <name>).

probe.description: One read-only shell command (an opaque string; $REPO_ROOT is substituted) whose exit 0 means the prerequisite is present. Any other exit, a probe that cannot start, and one still running after 30 seconds all mean absent. Resolvers compare no version or checksum: a record that needs a specific build writes a probe that checks it, against the pin the repo already keeps for CI.

hint.description: How a person provides the prerequisite, shown beside the skip. Display text only: resolvers never run it.

manager.description: The package manager that installs from the lockfile. npm is the only one.

lockfile.description: Repo-relative path of the lockfile: a package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json, with no leading slash and no '..' segment.

install.description: What the provisioning step installs for this entry: it runs npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund in the lockfile's directory, so no install script runs. The step runs at worktree creation (the source-control plugin's provision-prerequisites.sh), never inside a check: a resolver still only probes, and an entry the step could not install still reads skip (prerequisite missing: <name>). An entry without install is report-only.

run-from.description: Where the probe runs. 'repo-root' (default) runs it once from $REPO_ROOT. 'ecosystem' runs it from each location the command or gate cmd itself runs from, and the command is skipped only at the locations where the probe finds the prerequisite absent. This default differs from a gate's own run-from default: a probe inside a per-project gate still runs once from $REPO_ROOT unless the entry sets 'ecosystem'.
